title: Twenty First Word First Station Conclusion Wisdom In Calamity And Consolation Through Belief

questions.question: In the passage, what can happen when a person thinks only about this world?
questions.answer: A big joy can turn into deep sadness.

questions.question: In the village example, where had many of the first man's friends gone?
questions.answer: They had gone to Istanbul.

questions.question: About how many of the first man's friends had already left?
questions.answer: Almost all of them.

questions.question: How does the first man think about the place where his friends went?
questions.answer: He thinks of it as a good place and wants to go there too.

questions.question: How does the first man feel when he is told he can go there?
questions.answer: He feels very happy.

questions.question: What happened to many of the second man's friends?
questions.answer: He thinks they are gone in a terrible way.

questions.question: How does the second man try to make himself feel better?
questions.answer: He gets attached to one guest and looks for comfort in that.

questions.question: Why is the second man's comfort small and weak?
questions.answer: Because one person cannot replace all the others he lost.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the few people still alive here?
questions.answer: They will also go there later.

questions.question: How should a person face death, according to the passage?
questions.answer: With courage, not with fear.

questions.question: How should a person think about the grave, according to the passage?
questions.answer: He should face it honestly and not turn away.

questions.question: Which of the two men should a person avoid being like?
questions.answer: The second man.

questions.question: Does death change when times change?
questions.answer: No, death stays the same.

questions.question: Does human weakness go away over time, or does it grow?
questions.answer: It grows.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the human journey through life?
questions.answer: It keeps going and moves faster.

questions.question: Up to what point are other people with you?
questions.answer: Only up to the grave.

questions.question: Why is “everyone is in the same trouble” not a real comfort?
questions.answer: Because after the grave, that togetherness does not help.

questions.question: What does the world look like when seen with wisdom?
questions.answer: It looks ordered and full of purpose.

questions.question: According to the passage, are things in the world random and pointless?
questions.answer: No, they are not.

questions.question: What example from nature shows careful order on the earth?
questions.answer: Animals and plants are made and arranged in a very ordered way.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the earth’s movement?
questions.answer: It says the earth turns in an orderly way toward high goals.

questions.question: What wrong idea about earthquakes does the passage reject?
questions.answer: The idea that they are only chance and have no purpose.

questions.question: In the passage, by whose command do such events happen?
questions.answer: By the command of Allah, the All-Wise and All-Compassionate.

questions.question: What can happen to believers’ temporary property through such events?
questions.answer: It can become like charity and be made lasting in reward.

questions.question: How can such hard events help believers with their sins?
questions.answer: They can be a way of cleansing sins tied to thanklessness.

questions.question: What will the earth do one day to ugly deeds linked to shirk?
questions.answer: It will wipe them away and clean its face.

questions.question: What will be said to thankful people in the end?
questions.answer: They will be welcomed into Paradise.

questions.question: What is the main warning at the start of the passage about loving only this world?
questions.answer: It can change happiness into pain.

questions.question: In the story, what town is named as the place many friends went to?
questions.answer: Istanbul.

questions.question: Why does the first man want to go where his friends are?
questions.answer: Because the people he loves are there.

questions.question: What feeling fills the first man when he is allowed to go?
questions.answer: Joy.

questions.question: How does the second man think about the friends who left?
questions.answer: He thinks they are lost and gone forever in misery.

questions.question: What does this wrong thinking do to the second man’s heart?
questions.answer: It makes him sad and hurt by separation.

questions.question: Instead of remembering all his friends rightly, what does the second man hold on to?
questions.answer: One guest.

questions.question: What is said about the people still left in this world?
questions.answer: They will also go beyond the grave.

questions.question: What should a person not feel about death?
questions.answer: He should not be scared of it.

questions.question: What should a person not do when thinking about the grave?
questions.answer: He should not turn away from it.

questions.question: How should a person meet death instead?
questions.answer: Bravely.

questions.question: What excuse about modern life does the passage tell the nafs not to say?
questions.answer: That this age is different and everyone only chases worldly life.

questions.question: According to the passage, does separation ever become staying forever in this world?
questions.answer: No, it does not.

questions.question: What two human conditions are said to remain and even grow?
questions.answer: Weakness and need.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the speed of man’s journey?
questions.answer: It gets quicker.

questions.question: Why should a person not say, “I am just like everyone else”?
questions.answer: Because other people stay with you only for a short time.

questions.question: How far does people’s friendship go, as described here?
questions.answer: Up to the grave.

questions.question: When a person uses wisdom, what does he see in the world?
questions.answer: Order and purpose everywhere.

questions.question: Can a person really be outside Allah’s order and purpose?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What event does the passage use as an example when talking about the earth?
questions.answer: An earthquake.

questions.question: What does the passage say about calling earthquakes mere chance?
questions.answer: It says that is wrong.

questions.question: What picture is given to show the earth’s careful design?
questions.answer: It is dressed with layers of living things full of wisdom.

questions.question: Why is saying losses are for nothing a harmful idea?
questions.answer: Because it throws people into terrible hopelessness.

questions.question: What two bad things does the passage say such people are doing?
questions.answer: They are making a serious mistake and doing a serious wrong.

questions.question: What reward can come from believers losing worldly things in such events?
questions.answer: Their loss can count like charity that lasts.

questions.question: What final promise is given to thankful people?
questions.answer: They will be told to enter Paradise.

questions.question: What does the passage say can happen if someone looks only at worldly life?
questions.answer: Sweetness can become sorrow.

questions.question: In the example, how many of the first man’s friends are still in the village?
questions.answer: Only one is still there for now.

questions.question: Where are the first man’s other friends living?
questions.answer: In Istanbul.

questions.question: Why is the first man hopeful instead of hopeless?
questions.answer: Because he expects to join his friends.

questions.question: What does the first man do when he hears he may go to them?
questions.answer: He goes gladly.

questions.question: What does the second man imagine about those who left?
questions.answer: He imagines they are lost in a miserable way.

questions.question: How is the second man described because of this thinking?
questions.answer: He is very unhappy.

questions.question: What does he try to use instead of all his missing friends?
questions.answer: One guest.

questions.question: What truth about loved ones does the passage tell the nafs?
questions.answer: Loved ones are on the other side of the grave.

questions.question: What will happen to the one or two people still here?
questions.answer: They will go there too.

questions.question: What attitude toward the grave is taught in the passage?
questions.answer: A person should face it with courage.

questions.question: What warning is given about being heedless?
questions.answer: Do not be careless and act like the second man.

questions.question: What claim about changing times is rejected?
questions.answer: The claim that this age is so different that old truths no longer matter.

questions.question: Which fact of life does not change at all?
questions.answer: Death.

questions.question: What happens to human neediness and weakness?
questions.answer: They increase.

questions.question: Is the human trip through life stopping, or not?
questions.answer: It is not stopping.

questions.question: What does the passage say about depending on the crowd for comfort?
questions.answer: That comfort does not help after the grave.

questions.question: What kind of place is this world called?
questions.answer: A guesthouse.

questions.question: If someone looks at this guesthouse wisely, what will he notice?
questions.answer: Everything has arrangement and a reason.

questions.question: What question does the passage ask about being outside order?
questions.answer: It asks how a person could be without purpose when the world is not.

questions.question: What does the passage say earthquakes are not?
questions.answer: They are not toys of blind luck.

questions.question: What examples on earth show planning and beauty?
questions.answer: The many kinds of animals and plants.

questions.question: How is the earth’s turning described?
questions.answer: As very orderly and directed toward great aims.

questions.question: What feeling comes when people say losses in disasters have no reward?
questions.answer: Frightening despair.

questions.question: According to the passage, who sends such events with wisdom and mercy?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: For believers, what can their lost things become in reward?
questions.answer: They can become like sadaqah.

questions.question: Besides reward, what other benefit can these events bring to believers?
questions.answer: They can help erase sins from not being thankful enough.

questions.question: What will the earth do one day to works stained by shirk?
questions.answer: It will remove them and clean itself.

questions.question: What will happen to those who gave thanks?
questions.answer: They will be invited into Paradise.

questions.question: At the beginning of the passage, what mistake causes pleasure to turn into pain?
questions.answer: Caring only about worldly life.

questions.question: In the example of the two men, what is special about the first man’s many friends?
questions.answer: They have gone to another place where they are living well.

questions.question: What city is named in that example?
questions.answer: Istanbul.

questions.question: Why does the first man feel eager instead of crushed?
questions.answer: He believes he will join the people he loves.

questions.question: What happens to his feelings when travel to them becomes possible?
questions.answer: His heart becomes glad.

questions.question: How does the second man think about the ones who left?
questions.answer: He thinks they are gone in a sad and hopeless way.

questions.question: What does he do with a single guest?
questions.answer: He clings to that person for comfort.

questions.question: What big pain is he trying to hide from?
questions.answer: The pain of being separated from loved ones.

questions.question: Which person in the passage is a bad example to follow?
questions.answer: The second man.

questions.question: What does the passage say about friends and loved ones in relation to the grave?
questions.answer: They are there beyond it, and the rest will go there too.

questions.question: What kind of face should a person show to death?
questions.answer: A brave one.

questions.question: What should a person do instead of shrinking away from the grave?
questions.answer: Face it and think about its meaning.

questions.question: What worldly excuse does the nafs try to make about this age?
questions.answer: That people now are too busy with life and earning to focus on what matters.

questions.question: Does the passage agree that these changes cancel death and separation?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What human limits are still true in every age?
questions.answer: Human weakness and poverty of need.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the movement of life toward its end?
questions.answer: It says the journey becomes faster.

questions.question: Why is being “like everybody else” not enough?
questions.answer: Because the crowd cannot go with you past the grave.

questions.question: How long does ordinary friendship stay with a person, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Until the grave.

questions.question: What does wise looking show about the world?
questions.answer: That it is arranged and meaningful.

questions.question: What can be learned from the many layers of living things on earth?
questions.answer: They show careful making and wisdom.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the earth’s spinning?
questions.answer: To show it moves in order, not in chaos.

questions.question: What false idea about disasters is spoken against?
questions.answer: That they happen with no reason at all.

questions.question: What may an earthquake be compared to in the passage?
questions.answer: The earth shaking off forms of human heedlessness it dislikes.

questions.question: Why is it unfair to say the hurt of disaster victims is wasted?
questions.answer: Because their loss can have meaning and reward.

questions.question: What does the passage say believers’ lost property can become?
questions.answer: It can become lasting reward like charity.

questions.question: What can these trials do for sins linked to not thanking Allah enough?
questions.answer: They can serve as atonement.

questions.question: What will the earth think of works spoiled by shirk?
questions.answer: It will see them as ugly.

questions.question: What will happen to those who associated partners with Allah?
questions.answer: They will be cast into Hell.

questions.question: What will be said to those who are thankful?
questions.answer: They will be called to Paradise.

questions.question: What happens to joy when a person limits his thoughts to only this worldly life?
questions.answer: It turns into painful sadness.

questions.question: In the first example, what has happened to almost all of one man’s friends?
questions.answer: They have moved away to another place.

questions.question: What is the name of that place?
questions.answer: Istanbul.

questions.question: How does the first man feel about going where his friends are?
questions.answer: He strongly wants to go.

questions.question: What shows that the first man has hope?
questions.answer: He is happy when he hears he can go to them.

questions.question: How does the second man think about the friends who are gone?
questions.answer: He thinks they have vanished in misery.

questions.question: What sad choice does the second man make to ease his pain?
questions.answer: He settles for closeness with one visitor.

questions.question: What will happen to the few who are still living here?
questions.answer: They will leave and go there too.

questions.question: What emotion should a person fight when thinking about death?
questions.answer: Fear.

questions.question: How should a Muslim face death and the grave in this passage?
questions.answer: With courage and honesty.

questions.question: What warning is given against heedlessness?
questions.answer: Do not act like the hopeless second man.

questions.question: What common excuse about modern times is rejected?
questions.answer: The excuse that everyone is busy with worldly life, so that is just normal.

questions.question: Name one thing the passage says does not change.
questions.answer: Death.

questions.question: What happens to man’s weakness and need as time goes on?
questions.answer: They become greater.

questions.question: What happens to man’s journey through life?
questions.answer: It speeds up.

questions.question: Why can’t a person rely on “everyone else” for lasting support?
questions.answer: Because people part from him at the grave.

questions.question: What is the world called to remind us we are not staying forever?
questions.answer: A guesthouse.

questions.question: In this guesthouse, what does the eye of wisdom notice?
questions.answer: That everything has order and a purpose.

questions.question: What does the passage ask to show people are not free from purpose?
questions.answer: How can a person be purposeless when the world is full of purpose?

questions.question: Are earthquakes described as random accidents?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What picture of animals and plants helps show the earth’s order?
questions.answer: They are like beautifully arranged layers of clothing on the earth.

questions.question: What does the earth’s regular turning teach in the passage?
questions.answer: That it moves by order and wise aims.

questions.question: What bad result comes from saying disaster losses have no reward?
questions.answer: It puts people into terrible despair.

questions.question: What does the passage call that kind of thinking?
questions.answer: A great mistake and a great wrong.

questions.question: What can Allah turn believers’ temporary belongings into after such events?
questions.answer: Into lasting reward like alms.

questions.question: How can these events be mercy for believers besides reward?
questions.answer: They can wipe away sins.

questions.question: What will the earth do when it sees deeds spoiled by shirk?
questions.answer: It will clean them away from its face.

questions.question: What two different endings are named for two groups of people?
questions.answer: Those who made shirk go to Hell, and those who gave thanks enter Paradise.

questions.question: What is the first big lesson in the passage about focusing only on worldly life?
questions.answer: It changes pleasure into pain.

questions.question: In the story, what happened to nearly all of the first man’s friends?
questions.answer: They went to another city.

questions.question: Which city is mentioned?
questions.answer: Istanbul.

questions.question: Why does the first man keep thinking about that city?
questions.answer: Because his friends are there and he wants to be with them.

questions.question: What does he do when the chance comes to go?
questions.answer: He goes happily.

questions.question: What sad belief does the second man have about his absent friends?
questions.answer: He believes they are gone in a hopeless and miserable way.

questions.question: What does the second man use as a weak replacement for many friends?
questions.answer: One guest.

questions.question: What pain is still left in him?
questions.answer: The pain of separation.

questions.question: What should a person not do because of death and the grave?
questions.answer: He should not be terrified and turn away.

questions.question: What should he do instead?
questions.answer: He should face them bravely.

questions.question: Which man shows the wrong way of thinking?
questions.answer: The second man.

questions.question: What does the nafs say about the age that the passage corrects?
questions.answer: It says times are different and people are lost in worldly living.

questions.question: What answer does the passage give about death?
questions.answer: Death is still the same.

questions.question: What answer does it give about separation?
questions.answer: It does not become lasting life in this world.

questions.question: What answer does it give about human weakness and need?
questions.answer: They remain and even increase.

questions.question: What answer does it give about the journey of life?
questions.answer: It continues and becomes quicker.

questions.question: Why is it not enough to say, “I am with everyone else”?
questions.answer: Because others only accompany you to the grave.

questions.question: What kind of comfort is called meaningless after the grave?
questions.answer: The comfort of sharing disaster with everybody.

questions.question: When looking wisely at the world, what do we learn about it?
questions.answer: Nothing in it is without order or purpose.

questions.question: What does that teach about human life too?
questions.answer: Human life is not outside Allah’s order and purpose.

questions.question: What natural event is discussed to teach this lesson?
questions.answer: An earthquake.

questions.question: What does the passage say about calling such events chance?
questions.answer: It says that is false.

questions.question: How do the many kinds of living things on earth point to wisdom?
questions.answer: They are arranged beautifully and carefully for many purposes.

questions.question: How does the earth’s movement support the idea of order?
questions.answer: It turns in a regular way for lofty goals.

questions.question: What is wrong with saying the suffering of disaster victims is pointless?
questions.answer: It leads people into dark hopelessness and ignores possible reward.

questions.question: Under whose command do these events happen?
questions.answer: Under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What can happen to believers’ worldly losses because of Allah’s mercy?
questions.answer: They can become lasting reward like charity.

questions.question: What can these trials do about sins from being ungrateful?
questions.answer: They can make up for them.

questions.question: One day, how will the earth treat human works marked by shirk?
questions.answer: It will remove them from itself.

questions.question: What two final commands are mentioned at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Those with shirk are sent to Hell, and those who are thankful are invited to Paradise.
